own_solution.law: Hydrostatic equilibrium gives p_small - p_large = rho*g*h. Piston equilibrium therefore gives F = A1*((m*g/A2) + rho*g*h). With A1 = 0.002 m² and A2 = 0.08 m², F = 294 + 24.99 = 318.99 N downward. An additional supported mass q increases F by 0.0245*q N.
assumptions: The connected oil is at rest with uniform density.
The same atmospheric pressure acts on both outer piston faces.
The adjacent bottle jack is independent of the hydraulic lift.
The earlier-experiment-only load is absent from the present equilibrium.

defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: The numeral-free controls omit the 560 kg quantity required by the general variant-format instruction, although the authors explicitly disclose this intended difference and do not claim these controls preserve the numerical value.
